acquisition_method.evidence: inferred: Data acquisition was performed by alternating between full Fourier transform-mass spectrometry (FT-MS; 350–2000 m/z, resolution 60,000, 1 μscan per spectrum) and FT-MS/MS (150–2000 m/z, resolution 30,000, 1 μscan per spectrum) for the ten most intense ions above 500 count threshold with charge > + 2.

alkylation_concentration.evidence: Proteins were alkylated with 20 mM iodoacetamide at room temperature protected from the light during 45 min.
Peptides contained in distained gel pieces were reduced in 10 mM DTT in 25 mM ABB at 60 °C for 1 h and subsequently alkylated in 55 mM IAA in 25 mM ABB at room temperature for 45 min in the dark.

alkylation_reagent.evidence: Proteins were alkylated with 20 mM iodoacetamide at room temperature protected from the light during 45 min.

cleavage_agent.evidence: sequencing-grade-modified trypsin was purchased from Promega (Madison, WI, USA).
Tryptic digestion of proteins was performed overnight at 37 °C by the addition of 10 ng/μl of sequencing-grade-modified trypsin (prepared in 25 mM ABB buffer).

collision_energy.evidence: Fragmentation was performed using high-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) mode with 32% normalized collision energy.

fractionation_method.evidence: Reconstituted tryptic peptides after in-solution digestion were fractionated by a PolyWAX column (4.6 × 200 mm, 3 μm, PolyLC, Columbia, MD, USA) using a Shimadzu Prominence UFLC system (Kyoto, Japan).

fragmentation_method.evidence: Fragmentation was performed using high-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) mode with 32% normalized collision energy.

instrument.evidence: Analysis of peptides was performed using an Orbitrap Elite mass spectrometer coupled with a Dionex UltiMate 3000 UHPLC system from Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. (Bremen, Germany).

ionization_type.evidence: inferred: Tryptic-digested peptides were sprayed using a Bruker-Michrom Inc. Michrom’s Thermo Captive Spray nanoelectrospray ion source (Bruker-Michrom Inc., Auburn, CA, USA) with 1.5 kV spray voltage.
